item.title: These workers help train robots who could one day steal their jobs
item.description: Factory workers in India are being asked to wear GoPro cameras to record the way they do their jobs. The ultimate goal is to train robots to take over. Will it work?
item.content:encoded: Factory workers in India are being asked to wear GoPro cameras to record the way they do their jobs. The ultimate goal is to train robots to take over. Will it work?

item.title: Trump's ambassador to Greece, Kimberly Guilfoyle, resigns after allegations of improper conduct
item.description: The White House publicly asked for U.S. Ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle's resignation on Tuesday as she faced mounting accusations of improper conduct.

item.title: Civil rights advocates plan to send thousands of observers to midterm polling places
item.description: For many election cycles, civil rights groups and political parties have fanned out to monitor polling places, but the charged midterm environment has many organizations stepping up efforts this year.

item.title: The skincare sample is free. What happens next can cost thousands
item.description: For years, customers have complained of aggressive sales tactics and charges at mall skincare stores. NPR investigated the business that connects many of them.

item.title: The skincare scheme that led to consumer complaints, lawsuits and a federal investigation
item.description: Free samples, high-pressure pitches and $50,000 bills: An NPR investigation reveals how a network of mall skincare stores systematically targeted older adults and people with disabilities across the U.S..

item.title: 'They're stealing from the poor': A major source of SNAP fraud robs recipients of millions
item.description: Organized criminal rings target SNAP recipients because of the government program's outdated security features. But upgrading the tech costs money and states' SNAP budgets are getting squeezed.

item.title: In Kansas, a newly-competitive Senate race tests limit of Trump's unpopular policies
item.description: Kansas voters could send a Democrat to the Senate for the first time in nearly a century — and flip the governor's office back to Republican control, even in what could be a tough year for the GOP.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: CNN, MS NOW and Politico prevail against White House — for now
item.description: A federal judge ruled late Tuesday that President Trump cannot ban news organizations from covering him at the White House because he does not like the nature of their coverage - at least, not until the matter goes to a formal trial.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: Conservative super-lawyer squares up for his latest Supreme Court argument
item.description: Paul Clement, a Republican, has racked up dozens of wins at the Supreme Court since his days as George W. Bush's solicitor general. Recently, he's been challenging some Trump administration policies.
